title: Data Transformation Pipeline
definition: A data transformation pipeline separates the stages that receive, interpret, validate, transform, and present data.
purpose: Make trust boundaries, representation changes, failures, and output responsibilities inspectable.
history: Input-process-output models have long been used to explain computation; production pipelines refine the middle into explicit stages with contracts.
mental_model: Raw data crosses a boundary and moves through named gates; each gate either produces a more trustworthy representation or a controlled failure.
analogy: A quality-controlled production line transforms raw material through inspected stations; the analogy fails because software data can be copied, malformed, or context-dependent.
industry_notes: Pipeline stages need explicit input/output contracts, failure behavior, and observability without exposing sensitive data.
ai_notes: AI-generated pipelines must be checked for missing boundary cases, silent coercion, invented defaults, and unsafe error disclosure.
interview_notes: Ask the candidate to trace one value through receive, parse, validate, normalize, transform, and format stages.
exercise_candidates: Draw a transformation trace for a registration record
